newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: Trinidad's new budget hikes price of gas.
newsitem.headline: Trinidad's new budget hikes price of gas.

text.p: Finance Minister Brian Kuei Tung Thursday unveiled a $2.06 billion budget for 1997 that included a 1.7-cent hike in the price of gasoline, lower income taxes and increased pensions for senior citizens.
The fiscal package was based on a price of $20 for a barrel of oil, the minister said. Trinidad and Tobago, a twin-island nation of 1.3 million people, produces 129,000 barrels of oil a day.
People earning $6,333 and less a year would not pay income tax, Kuei Tung said in a 75-minute presentation to the House of Representatives.
Kuei Tung said four percent growth in the economy was projected. About 14,000 displaced workers were to be retrained and 25 new schools built over the next 12 months.
Opposition Leader Patrick Manning described the package as one which would benefit the middle class.
It was the second budget Kuei Tung delivered on behalf of the one-year-old coalition government led by Prime Minister Basdeo Panday.
Debate on the budget was scheduled to begin on Dec 17.
